newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico unveils public sector clean up plan.
newsitem.headline: Mexico unveils public sector clean up plan.

text.p: Mexico on Tuesday unveiled an environmental clean-up program for its polluting state-owned industries, pledging $633 million for the effort this year alone.

Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo announced the plan, promising that notorious polluters such as giant state oil and gas company Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) would soon become models of environmental care.
"Today I promise in front of all of you that before the end of my administration, all public companies will have efficient environmental management," he said at a ceremony.

Zedillo also announced a series of tax credits and tariff reductions for private companies that agree voluntarily to invest in environmentally friendly technology. He did not provide details of the new rules.

Pemex and the CFE have been accused by environmentalists in Mexico of massive environmental pollution. This week the international environmental group Greenpeace said Pemex was breaking international law by not dismantling unused oil rigs in the Gulf of Mexico that were leaking crude.
